//tcm: The TCM storage uses the same macro-backed wrapper as the timing flow (verif/gate/cdriscv_32s_20_tcm_macro.sv): two RM_IHPSG13_1P_2048x64 banks per TCM, so the arrays are silicon macros, not 320 kbit of flip-flops.
//timing: buf_4 + 0.35 resizer setup margins: the probe2 experiment measured the fetch critical path at -0.719 ns with buf_1 repair chains and -0.059 ns with buf_4 + 0.30; the extra 0.05 covers the remaining 59 ps over 2 endpoints.
//sdc: LibreLane's base.sdc constrains only the first clock and says so. This design has three (clk_i, ref_clk_i, tck_i); in the v2first run the other two were signed off with no constraint at all and ref_clk_i's 107 flops got a fanout-repair buffer chain instead of a CTS tree. flow/cdriscv_32s_20.sdc constrains all three and declares them asynchronous.
//clock: 40 ns = 25 MHz.  Chosen after the first full RTL2GDS run: the design met 20 ns at the typical corner but missed it by 9 ns at slow (1.08 V, 125 C), which is the corner a safety IP must sign off against (finding V45).
//drc: KLayout DRC rather than Magic: Magic's DRC is single-threaded and spent over three hours on one core of eight without finishing, while the IHP PDK ships its own KLayout deck (KLAYOUT_DRC_RUNSET in the PDK config) which threads and is the vendor's signoff deck for this process.
//lvs: The SRAM macro is black-boxed for LVS: its internals are vendor-verified, and the PDN physically straps VDD!/VSS!/VDDARRAY! on each of the four instances while the netlist blackbox declares no power ports -- twelve connections the layout has and the netlist cannot know about.  Without this, netgen reports devices matching exactly (96048 = 96048) with a 10-net difference and top-level pin matching failed.  With it: circuits match uniquely.
//floorplan: Memories in two rows (I-TCM south, D-TCM north) with the logic in the central band, rather than the four corners of a 2.9 mm die.  The corner placement put every macro ~2 mm from the logic, the clock tree spanned that distance, and 69 of 71 hold-critical endpoints were macro pins with 0.45 ns of skew (V45).  This also takes the die from 8.41 to 5.76 mm^2.
//die: Die 2400x3500: ring depth is 140 (sealring, PAD_EDGE_SPACING) + 180 (pad depth) per edge, core inset a further 30.  Sides hold S/E/N/W = 16/34/19/30 pads of 80 um; per-side fill checked against librelane pad_cfg.tcl arithmetic by the generator.
//sealring: DELIBERATELY DISABLED (2026-09-03): the PDK sealring PCell emits INT32_MIN far-coordinates for its edge arms on ALL 20 layers, for every size including the PDK docstring example (reproduce: sealring.py -rd width=1300.0 -rd height=1300.0), and the corrupt geometry crashes the density filler (KLayout dbPolygonGenerators m_open.empty). The die reserves the 140 um allowance via PAD_EDGE_SPACING, so the ring can be added post-fix without floorplan changes. Reported upstream; see doc/chip.md and verification_findings_20.md.
//pads: Pad instance lists are ordered: ascending x for south/north, ascending y for east/west.  Placement coordinates are computed by OpenROAD.PadRing (even spacing); this list order IS the placement data.
